edit.description: the default order taken from the filing times instead of the comparator it holds
the add-commit read the filing time needs

the filing times reaching every selection this tick takes
the ordering cases over a fixture repo with real add commits

summary: the engine reads each entry's filing time — the oldest commit that added a file under its tag — and the default order is that ascending, then tag
acceptance: a selection with no declared order serves the oldest-filed pickable work entry first, an entry no commit has added last, and breaks what remains on the tag
tests: the default order serves the oldest-filed entry first
an entry no commit has added yet is served last
re-filing an entry does not move it in the default order
two entries added by one commit break on the tag ascending
the filing time is the oldest commit that added a file under the tag, not the newest
notes: The read is git's, so it is per-selection state the engine holds and reports (`Chain.order`'s context carries it). One home, because the status flow figures read the same times.
